candidate_relations.reason: Meibomian gland dysfunction does not identify the autoimmune cicatrizing mucosal disease MMP and does not account for the characteristic progressive conjunctival fibrosis and symblepharon.

Ocular chronic graft-versus-host disease can cause conjunctival scarring and severe surface disease, but it is a distinct transplant-related etiology rather than MMP; no transplant history is supplied.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Alternative cause of cicatrizing ocular surface disease

candidate_relations.reason: Conjunctival scarring describes the observed fibrosis and symblepharon but omits the underlying diagnosis of mucous membrane pemphigoid.
Severe ocular surface disease is compatible with the presentation but lacks the specific autoimmune cicatrizing diagnosis of MMP.
Scleritis is inflammation of the sclera and does not correspond to the progressive cicatrizing conjunctival disease described or to MMP.
Atopic keratoconjunctivitis may cause chronic ocular surface inflammation and scarring but is a different disease from MMP, with no atopic basis provided.

case_quality_flags: Conjunctival immunofluorescence was nonspecific, but a nondiagnostic biopsy does not exclude clinically suspected MMP.
